proofs.proof_tex:
The first equivalence is \(\text{def:criterion}\), whose right-hand side is the finite incidence test \(\mathcal H(B)\ne\varnothing\) and does not invoke identification.  Suppose first that this set is nonempty.  By \(\text{thm:single-hazard-alternative}\), every compatible law satisfies
\[
Q(P)=\mathsf{Rec}^{(1)}_{T,k,j,B}((M_d(P))_{d=0}^T).
\tag{23}
\]
If \(\Phi_{T,S,B,e}(P)=\Phi_{T,S,B,e}(P')\), then \(\text{prop:audit-table-equivalence}\) gives \(M_d(P)=M_d(P')\) for every \(d\).  Applying the same deterministic map in (23) yields
\[
Q(P)=\mathsf{Rec}^{(1)}_{T,k,j,B}((M_d(P))_d)
=\mathsf{Rec}^{(1)}_{T,k,j,B}((M_d(P'))_d)=Q(P').
\]
This is precisely \(\operatorname{GID}(T,S,B)=1\) by \(\text{def:graphwise-identification}\).

Conversely, if \(\mathcal H(B)=\varnothing\), the obstruction branch of \(\text{thm:single-hazard-alternative}\) supplies \(P,P'\in\mathcal P_{T,S,B,e}\) having equal observed laws and unequal endpoint vectors.  This pair violates the implication in \(\text{def:graphwise-identification}\), so \(\operatorname{GID}(T,S,B)=0\).  This proves the second equivalence and identifies the outputs of both branches.  The recovery proof used only positive scalar normalization and Markov factorization, not transition-matrix inversion, so deficient ranks and null allowed-arrow effects are included.

By \(\text{def:criterion}\), a design succeeds exactly when it contains at least one incidence \((d,\ell)\) with \(0\le d<k\) and \(j\le\ell\le T\).  If a successful design contains two or more audited incidences, or contains one such incidence together with any other audited coordinate, deleting all but one successful incidence gives a strictly smaller successful design.  It is therefore not inclusion-minimal.  Conversely, a design containing exactly one coordinate \(B_d=\{\ell\}\) with \(d<k\) and \(\ell\ge j\) loses its only member of \(\mathcal H(B)\) after any strict deletion, so it is minimal.  There are \(k\) choices of \(d\in\{0,\ldots,k-1\}\) and \(T-j+1\) choices of \(\ell\in\{j,\ldots,T\}\); all are legal because \(d<k\le j\le\ell\).  This proves the displayed family and its cardinality.

For each \(d<T\), there are \(T-d\) independently includable post-dropout coordinates.  Hence the number of bundle designs is
\[
2^{\sum_{d=0}^{T-1}(T-d)}=2^{T(T+1)/2}.
\]
Exhaustive evaluation of the finite incidence test and deletion of every nonminimal success therefore returns exactly the family just proved, which agrees with \(\text{def:minimal-frontier}\).

If \(B\le B'\), every incidence present in \(B\) is present in \(B'\), whence \(\mathcal H(B)\subseteq\mathcal H(B')\); criterion monotonicity follows immediately.  For the supporting graphwise statement, suppose two laws have the same observed law under \(B'\).  By \(\text{prop:audit-table-equivalence}\), their \(B'\)-pattern tables agree.  Marginalizing each such table over the coordinates in \(B'_d\setminus B_d\) gives the corresponding \(B\)-pattern table, so those tables also agree.  A second use of \(\text{prop:audit-table-equivalence}\) gives equality of the observed laws under \(B\).  Thus \(\operatorname{GID}(T,S,B)=1\) implies \(\operatorname{GID}(T,S,B')=1\), as claimed.

The displayed incidence condition is exactly \(\mathcal H(B)\ne\varnothing\).  The scan length and the two constructive outputs follow from \(\text{thm:single-hazard-alternative}\), while
\[
\mathsf C_1=1\Longleftrightarrow\mathcal H(B)\ne\varnothing
\Longleftrightarrow\operatorname{GID}(T,S,B)=1
\]
is \(\text{thm:constructive-completeness}\).  Finally, \(\text{thm:minimal-design-frontier}\) proves that a minimal success contains exactly one such incidence and no extraneous audited coordinate.  These three cited results supply respectively the explicit reconstruction or witness, the necessary-and-sufficient causal conclusion, and the exact frontier.

Because \(\mathsf C_1=1\), the set \(\mathcal H(B)\) is nonempty by \(\text{def:criterion}\), and its lexicographically first pair \((d,\ell)\) depends only on the fixed design.  Equations (1)--(11) in \(\text{thm:single-hazard-alternative}\) express every coordinate of the returned reconstruction using finite sums, products, and ratios of pattern-table cells.  At a positive population law, all denominator functionals in (3)--(5) and (9) are strictly positive.  There is therefore an open neighborhood of the population table on which the same denominators remain nonzero.  On this neighborhood the reconstruction is rational and hence continuously differentiable with a finite derivative.

By \(\text{prop:audit-table-equivalence}\), known positive audit probabilities map the observed-cell vector to the pattern tables by a fixed finite linear transformation: audited cells are divided by the corresponding \(e_d(H_d)>0\), and the required routine marginals are finite sums.  Composing this linear map with the rational reconstruction gives the stated local map \(F\).  The recovery part of \(\text{thm:single-hazard-alternative}\) proves the population identity
\[
F(o)=Q;
\tag{24}
\]
it is not imposed by the definition of \(F\).

For consistency, enumerate the \(m\) structural observed cells.  By \(\text{ass:iid-sampling}\), each coordinate is an average of iid Bernoulli indicators, so
\[
\operatorname{Var}(\widehat o_{n,r})
=\frac{o_r(1-o_r)}n\le\frac1{4n}.
\]
For each \(r\), the pointwise inequality
\[
(\widehat o_{n,r}-o_r)^2
\ge\delta^2\mathbf 1\{|\widehat o_{n,r}-o_r|>\delta\}
\]
implies the corresponding probability bound after taking expectations.  Summing these bounds over the finite cells gives, for every \(\delta>0\),
\[
\Pr\{\|\widehat o_n-o\|_\infty>\delta\}
\le\sum_{r=1}^m
\frac{\operatorname{Var}(\widehat o_{n,r})}{\delta^2}
\le\frac{m}{4n\delta^2}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{25}
\]
For every \(\eta>0\), continuity of \(F\) at \(o\) supplies a \(\delta>0\) such that \(\|v-o\|<\delta\) implies \(\|F(v)-F(o)\|<\eta\).  Equation (25), followed by (24), therefore proves \(F(\widehat o_n)\to Q\) in probability whenever the rational formula is defined.  Define the estimator arbitrarily when an empirical denominator vanishes.  Since every population denominator is positive, (25) shows that the probability of this modification tends to zero.

For the limit law, the cited finite-multinomial central limit theorem gives
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat o_n-o)\Rightarrow
N\!\left(0,\operatorname{diag}(o)-oo^\top\right).
\tag{26}
\]
Finally, the cited multivariate delta method applied to (26) yields
\[
\sqrt n\{F(\widehat o_n)-F(o)\}\Rightarrow
N\!\left(0,DF(o)[\operatorname{diag}(o)-oo^\top]DF(o)^\top\right).
\]
Substitution of the proved identity (24) gives the asserted centering at the causal target.  If one starts from inverse-probability audit tables, the initial table estimator is the same fixed linear image of \(\widehat o_n\); the chain rule composes \(DF(o)\) with that linear map, proving the final assertion.

theorem.statement:
Suppose \(S_k=\{j\}\), where \(j\in\{k,k+1\}\cap\{1,\ldots,T\}\), and \(S_t=\varnothing\) for \(t\ne k\).  The finite procedure \(\mathsf A_1\) terminates after scanning \(\mathcal H(B)\).  If \(\mathcal H(B)\ne\varnothing\), it returns an evaluable rational map \(\mathsf{Rec}^{(1)}_{T,k,j,B}\) such that
\[
\mathsf{Rec}^{(1)}_{T,k,j,B}((M_d(P))_{d=0}^T)=Q(P)
\]
for every \(P\in\mathcal P_{T,S,B,e}\).  If \(\mathcal H(B)=\varnothing\), it returns two strictly positive laws \((P,P')=\mathsf{Wit}^{(1)}_{T,k,j,B}\) in \(\mathcal P_{T,S,B,e}\) with
\[
\Phi_{T,S,B,e}(P)=\Phi_{T,S,B,e}(P')
\quad\text{and}\quad Q(P)\ne Q(P').
\]
The construction is valid for every specified finite alphabet, every horizon \(T\), null effects on allowed arrows, and transition kernels of arbitrary rank.
theorem.proof_tex:
Fix the graph in the statement.  For notational clarity, condition temporarily on a cell \((W=w,A=a)\).  This cell and every dropout stratum have positive probability by \(\text{ass:substantive-positivity}\), \(\text{ass:hazard-positivity}\), and the factorization in \(\text{ass:substantive-markov}\).  Write \(q_t(w,a)=\gamma_t(w,a)\in(0,1)\) for \(t\ne k\); these hazards are constant in the substantive trajectory by \(\text{ass:local-hazards}\).

We first give the recovery branch.  All its ingredients are explicit functions of the pattern tables.  With \(I_T=\{1,\ldots,T\}\), define the stratum masses
\[
\tau_r(w,a)=\sum_{x_{I_r}}M_r(w,a,x_{I_r}),\qquad 0\le r\le T,
\tag{1}
\]
and recover
\[
p_W(w)=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\sum_{r=0}^T\tau_r(w,a).
\tag{2}
\]
If \(\ell\in B_d\), define the audited conditional marginal
\[
A_{d,\ell}(z\mid w,a)
=\frac{\displaystyle
\sum_{x_{I_d\setminus\{\ell\}}}M_d(w,a,x_{I_d})
}{\tau_d(w,a)}.
\tag{3}
\]
From complete cases define
\[
C_\ell(z\mid w,a)
=\frac{\displaystyle\sum_{x_{1:T}:x_\ell=z}M_T(w,a,x_{1:T})}
{\tau_T(w,a)}
\tag{4}
\]
and
\[
L_{\ell,w,a}(x\mid z)
=\frac{\displaystyle
\sum_{x_{1:T}:x_\ell=z,\,x_T=x}M_T(w,a,x_{1:T})
}{\displaystyle
\sum_{x_{1:T}:x_\ell=z}M_T(w,a,x_{1:T})}.
\tag{5}
\]
When \(\ell=T\), (5) is the identity kernel.  Each denominator in (3)--(5) is strictly positive: every substantive trajectory has positive mass, every factor selecting its dropout stratum is positive, and the sums are finite and nonempty.

On \(D=T\), the conditional trajectory mass given \((w,a)\) is proportional to
\[
K_1(x_1\mid w,a)\prod_{t=2}^T K_t(x_t\mid w,a,x_{t-1})q_k(w,a,x_j),
\tag{6}
\]
because the remaining factors \(\prod_{t\ne k}\gamma_t(w,a)\) are constant.  For \(\ell\ge j\), condition on \(X_\ell=z\) in (6).  The sum of all factors through visit \(\ell\), including \(q_k(w,a,x_j)\), is then a common positive normalizing factor, whereas the suffix is
\[
\prod_{t=\ell+1}^T K_t(x_t\mid w,a,x_{t-1}).
\]
Normalization cancels the prefix factor.  Consequently
\[
L_{\ell,w,a}(x\mid z)
=\Pr(X_T=x\mid X_\ell=z,W=w,A=a).
\tag{7}
\]
This is a direct Markov-factorization calculation and uses no inversion or rank condition.

Let \((d,\ell)\) be the lexicographically first member of \(\mathcal H(B)\).  If \(d\le k-2\), the dropout event \(D=d\) has, conditional on \((w,a,X)\), the factor
\[
\left\{\prod_{s=1}^d\gamma_s(w,a)\right\}
\{1-\gamma_{d+1}(w,a)\},
\]
which does not depend on \(X\).  Hence
\[
\pi_{\ell,w,a}(z):=A_{d,\ell}(z\mid w,a)
=\Pr(X_\ell=z\mid W=w,A=a).
\tag{8}
\]

It remains to handle \(d=k-1\).  Define, using (1),
\[
\rho_{w,a}
=\frac{\displaystyle\sum_{r=k}^T\tau_r(w,a)}
{\displaystyle\sum_{r=k-1}^T\tau_r(w,a)}
=\Pr(D\ge k\mid W=w,A=a,D\ge k-1).
\tag{9}
\]
The denominator is positive and \(0<\rho_{w,a}<1\) by hazard positivity.  The event \(D\ge k-1\) involves only the constants \(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_{k-1}\), and is therefore independent of \(X\) given \((w,a)\).  Conditional on \(D\ge k\), all further continuation factors are constants, so the law of \(X_\ell\) is the same as its law conditional on \(D=T\), namely (4).  Partitioning \(D\ge k-1\) into \(D=k-1\) and \(D\ge k\) therefore gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\pi_{\ell,w,a}(z)
&:=(1-\rho_{w,a})A_{k-1,\ell}(z\mid w,a)
+\rho_{w,a}C_\ell(z\mid w,a)\\
&=\Pr(X_\ell=z\mid W=w,A=a).
\end{aligned}
\tag{10}
\]
Equations (2), (5), (8), and (10) define the returned map by
\[
\mathsf{Rec}^{(1)}_{T,k,j,B}((M_r)_{r=0}^T)_a(x)
=\sum_{w\in\mathcal W}p_W(w)
\sum_{z\in\mathcal X_\ell}
\pi_{\ell,w,a}(z)L_{\ell,w,a}(x\mid z).
\tag{11}
\]
Using (7) and the law of total probability in (11) yields
\[
\sum_w p_W(w)\Pr(X_T=x\mid W=w,A=a)
=Q_a(x),
\tag{12}
\]
where the last equality is the truncated substantive factorization in \(\text{def:causal-target}\).  Thus (11) is an observed-law functional whose equality to the causal target has been derived, not stipulated.  The calculation applies simultaneously to every \(a\) and \(x\), to null allowed-arrow effects, and to deficient transition ranks.

We now construct the obstruction branch.  Suppose \(\mathcal H(B)=\varnothing\).  Choose the first enumerated baseline cell \(w_\star\) and the first enumerated treatment cell \(a_\star\).  Keep a common strictly positive \(p_W\), a common strictly positive \(p_A\), and identical kernels and hazards outside this cell.  On every alphabet \(\mathcal X_r\), choose a strictly positive reference mass \(\nu_r\) and a nonconstant function \(h_r\) satisfying
\[
\sum_y\nu_r(y)h_r(y)=0,
\qquad |h_r(y)|\le1.
\tag{13}
\]
Such a pair exists because \(|\mathcal X_r|\ge2\): the procedure takes \(\nu_r\) uniform, assigns \(h_r=1\) and \(h_r=-1\) to the first two enumerated cells, and assigns zero to the rest.  It fixes \(\epsilon=1/2\), and on \(\mathcal X_j\) sets
\[
\mu(z)=\nu_j(z)\{1+\epsilon h_j(z)\},
\qquad
\mu'(z)=\nu_j(z)\{1-\epsilon h_j(z)\}.
\tag{14}
\]
Centering in (13) makes both vectors normalized; boundedness and \(\epsilon<1\) make them strictly positive.  They are distinct because \(h_j\) is nonconstant.  Put
\[
c(z)=\frac12\min\{\mu(z),\mu'(z)\},
\qquad
q_k(w_\star,a_\star,z)=\frac{c(z)}{\mu(z)},
\qquad
q'_k(w_\star,a_\star,z)=\frac{c(z)}{\mu'(z)}.
\tag{15}
\]
Then both hazards lie strictly between zero and one.  Take every other hazard to be a common constant in \((0,1)\).

Choose common positive kernels before visit \(j\), for example kernels that ignore their predecessor and have laws \(\nu_r\).  At \((w_\star,a_\star)\), let the visit-\(j\) kernel ignore its predecessor and equal \(\mu\) in the first model and \(\mu'\) in the second.  For \(r>j\), use in both models, with \(\lambda_r=1/2\),
\[
K_r(y\mid w_\star,a_\star,z)
=\nu_r(y)\{1+\lambda_r h_{r-1}(z)h_r(y)\},
\qquad \lambda_r=1/2.
\tag{16}
\]
Equation (13) shows that (16) sums to one in \(y\), and the bounds in (13) and \(\lambda_r<1\) show that every entry is strictly positive.  Moreover,
\[
\mathbb E\{h_r(X_r)\mid X_{r-1}=z,W=w_\star,A=a_\star\}
=\lambda_r h_{r-1}(z)\sigma_r^2,
\qquad
\sigma_r^2:=\sum_y\nu_r(y)h_r(y)^2>0.
\tag{17}
\]
At visit \(j\), (14) gives
\[
\mathbb E_\mu h_j-\mathbb E_{\mu'}h_j
=2\epsilon\sigma_j^2>0.
\tag{18}
\]
Iterating (17), the difference between the two interventional endpoint expectations of \(h_T\), conditional on \(w_\star\) and intervention \(A=a_\star\), is
\[
2\epsilon\sigma_j^2
\prod_{r=j+1}^T\lambda_r\sigma_r^2>0,
\tag{19}
\]
where an empty product is one.  All other baseline cells are common, so after averaging over \(W\) the difference is multiplied by \(p_W(w_\star)>0\).  Therefore the endpoint distributions differ in at least one cell, and hence \(Q(P)\ne Q(P')\).

It remains to verify equality of every observed table.  For every dropout index \(r\ge k\), the full subdensity is pointwise equal in the two models because the only changed substantive--response product is
\[
\mu(z)q_k(w_\star,a_\star,z)
=c(z)
=\mu'(z)q'_k(w_\star,a_\star,z).
\tag{20}
\]
Thus \(M_r=M'_r\) for \(r\ge k\).  If \(r\le k-2\), failure of \(\mathcal H(B)\) implies that every coordinate in \(I_r\) is smaller than \(j\).  The two models have the same law on those coordinates, and summing the normalized changed suffix from visit \(j\) onward gives one in both models.  Thus \(M_r=M'_r\).  Finally, every coordinate in \(I_{k-1}\) is also smaller than \(j\), while marginalizing the visit-\(j\) factor and the normalized downstream tail gives
\[
\sum_z\mu(z)\{1-q_k(w_\star,a_\star,z)\}
=1-\sum_zc(z)
=\sum_z\mu'(z)\{1-q'_k(w_\star,a_\star,z)\}.
\tag{21}
\]
Hence \(M_{k-1}=M'_{k-1}\) as well.  All other \((w,a)\) cells were held fixed.  The already-established \(\text{prop:audit-table-equivalence}\), using the same known \(e\), now gives
\[
\Phi_{T,S,B,e}(P)=\Phi_{T,S,B,e}(P').
\tag{22}
\]

Every substantive entry in the construction is positive by (13)--(16), and every hazard and failure probability is positive by (15) and the choice of the remaining constants.  Independent uniform disturbances, transformed by the inverse cumulative probabilities of the displayed finite kernels, realize these tables with mutually independent substantive and response noises.  Thus both laws lie in \(\mathcal P_{T,S,B,e}\) and respect the specified parent sets; ignored allowed parents are null effects.  The scan has only \(k(T-j+1)\) entries and the witness uses finitely many table entries, so \(\mathsf A_1\) terminates on both branches.  This proves the exhaustive single-hazard alternative.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Suppose \(S_k=\{j\}\), where \(j\in\{k,k+1\}\cap\{1,\ldots,T\}\), and \(S_t=\varnothing\) for \(t\ne k\). Then \(\mathsf C_1=1\) if and only if \(\mathcal H(B)\ne\varnothing\), if and only if \(\operatorname{GID}(T,S,B)=1\). The affirmative branch returns the explicit reconstruction and the negative branch returns the positive witness, uniformly over all positive laws, null allowed-arrow effects, and deficient transition ranks.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The undefined multi-hazard certificate has no proved exhaustive rule system. The complete recovery-or-witness theorem is proved for the strict subclass with exactly one substantively informative hazard; the new criterion is an explicit audit-incidence test rather than a restatement of graphwise identification.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: For the single-informative-hazard graph, the frontier consists exactly of the \(k(T-j+1)\) designs having \(B_d=\{\ell\}\) for one pair \(0\le d<k\), \(j\le\ell\le T\), and every other bundle empty. Exhaustive testing of the finite incidence criterion returns this family; \(B\le B'\) implies \(\mathcal H(B)\subseteq\mathcal H(B')\), and graphwise identification remains monotone under enlargement of audit bundles.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The old statement depended on the unavailable arbitrary-local-graph equivalence. The exact antichain and criterion monotonicity are completely derivable in the single-hazard subclass.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: In the single-informative-hazard graph, \(\mathsf A_1\) terminates after \(k(T-j+1)\) checks and \(\mathsf C_1=1\) exactly when some \(d<k\) audits some \(X_\ell\) with \(\ell\ge j\). The successful branch uses the explicit audited-marginal or risk-set reconstruction, the failure branch uses the explicit positive scaling witness, and the minimal designs are exactly the singleton incidences.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The prior graphwise reduction was already proved, but its reference to the undefined general criterion was not. Replacing that symbol by the explicit single-hazard scan closes the proposition constructively.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: For a successful single-hazard design, the deterministic \(\mathsf A_1\) reconstruction is rational and continuously differentiable with finite derivative at every positive population law, equals \(Q\) there, and its empirical observed-cell plug-in estimator is consistent and asymptotically Gaussian with covariance \(DF(o)[\operatorname{diag}(o)-oo^\top]DF(o)^\top\). The known-\(e\) audit-table form follows by composition with its fixed linear map.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The unresolved general reconstruction could only support a conditional regular-branch statement. The explicit single-hazard formulas have positive denominators at every legal population law, so smoothness and correct causal centering are now proved without a rank qualification.

proposed.name: Finite single-hazard recovery-or-obstruction procedure
proposed.construction:
For the single-informative-hazard graph specified by an index \(k\) and a parent \(j\in\{k,k+1\}\cap\{1,\ldots,T\}\), with \(S_k=\{j\}\) and \(S_t=\varnothing\) for \(t\ne k\), put
\[
\mathcal H(B)=\{(d,\ell):0\le d<k,\ j\le\ell\le T,\ \ell\in B_d\}.
\]
The procedure \(\mathsf A_1(T,k,j,B,(|\mathcal X_t|)_{t=1}^T)\) scans these \(k(T-j+1)\) pairs in lexicographic order.  If \(\mathcal H(B)\ne\varnothing\), it selects the first pair \((d,\ell)\).  Write \(\Pr_M\) for probabilities and conditional probabilities obtained by summing and positively normalizing the tables \((M_r)_{r=0}^T\).  The returned map uses
\[
L_{\ell,w,a}(x\mid z)=\Pr_M(X_T=x\mid X_\ell=z,W=w,A=a,D=T)
\]
and
\[
\pi_{\ell,w,a}(z)=
\begin{cases}
\Pr_M(X_\ell=z\mid W=w,A=a,D=d),&d\le k-2,\\
(1-\rho_{w,a})\Pr_M(X_\ell=z\mid W=w,A=a,D=k-1)
+\rho_{w,a}\Pr_M(X_\ell=z\mid W=w,A=a,D=T),&d=k-1,
\end{cases}
\]
where
\[
\rho_{w,a}=\frac{\Pr_M(W=w,A=a,D\ge k)}{\Pr_M(W=w,A=a,D\ge k-1)}.
\]
It outputs
\[
\mathsf{Rec}^{(1)}_{T,k,j,B}((M_r)_{r=0}^T)_a(x)
=\sum_w\Pr_M(W=w)\sum_{z\in\mathcal X_\ell}
\pi_{\ell,w,a}(z)L_{\ell,w,a}(x\mid z).
\]
If \(\mathcal H(B)=\varnothing\), use the specified enumeration of each alphabet: take \(\nu_r\) uniform, let \(h_r\) equal \(1\) and \(-1\) on the first two cells and zero on the rest, and set \(\epsilon=1/2\) and \(\lambda_r=1/2\).  At the first enumerated \((w,a)\) cell set
\[
\mu=\nu_j(1+\epsilon h_j),\qquad
\mu'=\nu_j(1-\epsilon h_j),\qquad
c(z)=\tfrac12\min\{\mu(z),\mu'(z)\},
\]
\[
q_k(z)=c(z)/\mu(z),\qquad q'_k(z)=c(z)/\mu'(z),
\]
and use the common downstream kernels
\[
K_r(y\mid z)=\nu_r(y)\{1+\lambda_r h_{r-1}(z)h_r(y)\},\qquad r>j.
\]
All other primitive tables are fixed common positive tables.  These formulas define the returned pair \(\mathsf{Wit}^{(1)}_{T,k,j,B}\); their recovery and obstruction properties are proved in \(\text{thm:single-hazard-alternative}\).  Thus the procedure has no rank, optimization, or iterative branch.

proposed.name: Single-hazard audit-incidence criterion
proposed.construction:
For \(S_k=\{j\}\), \(j\in\{k,k+1\}\cap\{1,\ldots,T\}\), and \(S_t=\varnothing\) for \(t\ne k\), define
\[
\mathsf C_1(T,k,j,B,(|\mathcal X_t|)_{t=1}^T)=1
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\mathcal H(B)\ne\varnothing.
\]
Equivalently, \(\mathsf C_1=1\) exactly when the finite scan \(\mathsf A_1\) returns its recovery branch.  This definition does not refer to \(\operatorname{GID}\).

proposed.statement:
Suppose \(S_k=\{j\}\), where \(j\in\{k,k+1\}\cap\{1,\ldots,T\}\), and \(S_t=\varnothing\) for \(t\ne k\).  Then
\[
\mathsf C_1(T,k,j,B,(|\mathcal X_t|)_{t=1}^T)=1
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\mathcal H(B)\ne\varnothing
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{GID}(T,S,B)=1.
\]
On the affirmative branch \(\mathsf A_1\) returns \(\mathsf{Rec}^{(1)}_{T,k,j,B}\), and on the negative branch it returns \(\mathsf{Wit}^{(1)}_{T,k,j,B}\).  The equivalence holds for the entire vector \((Q_a(x))_{a,x}\), for every positive compatible law, including null allowed-arrow effects and transition kernels of deficient rank.
proposed.justification: The explicit iff separates a genuine design rule from a sufficient recipe and makes failure operational through a legal positive countermodel.
proposed.gap: Existing monotone-MNAR results do not characterize which partial audits identify the intervention endpoint even in this arbitrary-horizon single-informative-hazard family.
proposed.consumer: A longitudinal study can decide whether a proposed pre-hazard dropout audit supports every treatment-specific endpoint probability under the declared single-hazard graph.

proposed.statement: For the single-informative-hazard graph \(S_k=\{j\}\), \(j\in\{k,k+1\}\cap\{1,\ldots,T\}\), and \(S_t=\varnothing\) for \(t\ne k\), the frontier \(\mathfrak F_1\) consists exactly of the \(k(T-j+1)\) designs for which one pair \((d,\ell)\), with \(0\le d<k\) and \(j\le\ell\le T\), has \(B_d=\{\ell\}\) and every other bundle is empty.  Testing \(\mathsf C_1\) on all \(2^{T(T+1)/2}\) designs and deleting nonminimal successes returns this family.  If \(B\le B'\), then \(\mathcal H(B)\subseteq\mathcal H(B')\), so \(\mathsf C_1(B)=1\) implies \(\mathsf C_1(B')=1\).  More generally, graphwise identification is monotone under enlargement of audit bundles.
proposed.justification: The focal design output is the complete finite antichain of irreducible sufficient audits in the proved subclass.
proposed.gap: Existing monotone-MNAR and double-sampling results do not enumerate minimal partial-recovery designs by dropout stratum.
proposed.consumer: Investigators can compare exactly \(k(T-j+1)\) irreducible protocols before assigning chart-abstraction or tracing costs.

proposed.statement:
Suppose exactly one continuation hazard may depend on a substantive state: \(S_k=\{j\}\), where \(j\in\{k,k+1\}\cap\{1,\ldots,T\}\), and \(S_t=\varnothing\) for \(t\ne k\).  Then \(\mathsf A_1\) terminates after \(k(T-j+1)\) incidence checks and
\[
\mathsf C_1=1
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\text{there are }d<k\text{ and }\ell\ge j\text{ with }\ell\in B_d.
\]
On success it uses the audited marginal or risk-set mixture and the complete-case Markov tail; on failure it uses the positive mass--hazard scaling witness.  The inclusion-minimal sufficient designs have \(B_d=\{\ell\}\) for exactly one pair \(d<k\le j\le\ell\), with all other bundles empty.
proposed.justification: This gives a closed-form arbitrary-horizon measurement rule, recovery, and positive obstruction for the complete single-hazard subclass.
proposed.gap: The passive self-censoring obstruction in the anchor does not state exactly which downstream partial audit destroys its cancellation.
proposed.consumer: Scientific knowledge isolating one informative dropout hazard translates directly into a finite list of sufficient measurements.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The reduction is made constructive by naming the finite scan, reconstruction, and witness that are now proved.

proposed.statement:
Suppose \(S_k=\{j\}\), where \(j\in\{k,k+1\}\cap\{1,\ldots,T\}\), \(S_t=\varnothing\) for \(t\ne k\), and \(\mathsf C_1=1\).  Let \(F\) be the composition of the known-\(e\) linear audit-table map with the deterministic rational reconstruction returned by \(\mathsf A_1\).  At every positive population law, \(F\) has a continuously differentiable local extension with finite derivative and \(F(o)=Q\).  For iid records,
\[
F(\widehat o_n)\longrightarrow Q\quad\text{in probability},
\]
and
\[
\sqrt n\{F(\widehat o_n)-Q\}\Rightarrow
N\!\left(0,DF(o)[\operatorname{diag}(o)-oo^\top]DF(o)^\top\right).
\]
The same conclusion holds when the reconstruction is presented in terms of inverse-probability audit tables, after composing its derivative with the fixed known-\(e\) linear map.
proposed.justification: The explicit rational identification map yields consistent finite-table plug-in estimation and a joint Gaussian law at every positive population point.
proposed.gap: Full-follow-up double-sampling theory does not provide the derivative of this partial-bundle reconstruction.
proposed.consumer: A sufficient partial-audit design obtains standard errors for every treatment-specific endpoint probability without recovering the complete missing trajectory.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The explicit single-hazard reconstruction is rational with positive population denominators, so regularity is proved at every legal population law and the limit is centered at the causal target.

prose_updates.tldr: For the complete arbitrary-horizon subclass with exactly one substantively informative continuation hazard, a finite audit-incidence scan is necessary and sufficient for identifying the entire endpoint intervention distribution. A successful scan returns an explicit rational reconstruction from one audited pre-hazard dropout marginal, a risk-set mixture when needed, and a complete-case Markov tail; a failed scan returns two strictly positive graph-compatible SCMs with identical observed laws and different endpoint interventions. The exact minimal frontier contains \(k(T-j+1)\) singleton audit designs. Empirical plug-in estimation is smooth at every positive law, while observed-cell projection retains finite-sample coverage beyond identified designs. Interacting multi-hazard completeness is left to future work.

project_justification.gap: Passive monotone-MNAR theory gives local recovery formulas and self-censoring obstructions, while randomized double-sampling theory typically completes the missing record. Neither gives a necessary-and-sufficient partial-audit rule for the endpoint intervention distribution in an arbitrary-horizon chain with one current- or lead-state-dependent hazard.
project_justification.niche: The single-informative-hazard graph family is broad in horizon, alphabet sizes, audit bundles, null allowed-arrow effects, and transition rank, yet its response fiber admits a complete incidence alternative with an explicit positive obstruction.
project_justification.fill: A finite scan of \(\mathcal H(B)=\{(d,\ell):d<k,\ell\ge j,\ell\in B_d\}\) returns either a rational endpoint reconstruction or a strictly positive observational-equivalence witness, proves \(\mathsf C_1=\operatorname{GID}\) on this complete subclass, and enumerates all \(k(T-j+1)\) minimal designs.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Use empirical observed-cell frequencies or Horvitz--Thompson audit-pattern tables with known \(e_d\); on a successful single-hazard design, apply the deterministic rational reconstruction selected by \(\mathsf A_1\).

prose_updates.related_work: Tikka and Karvanen (2025) establish monotone-missingness recoveries and a mediated self-censoring nonidentification construction, but do not decide which same-subject partial audits identify an endpoint intervention distribution. The present theorem closes that audit-design question for the arbitrary-horizon single-informative-hazard subclass, not for interacting local hazards. Tikka and Karvanen (2024) study rank conditions for categorical colluder propensities; the present reconstruction uses no transition-rank premise. Levis et al. (2024) identify smooth complete-data functionals after randomized intensive follow-up that completes the coarsened record, whereas the sufficient singleton audits here may recover neither the full trajectory nor the endpoint. Guo and Nabi (2026) give a sound intervention-tree construction without the completeness claim made here for this restricted graph family. Duarte et al. (2024) supply finite polynomial optimization machinery used only for projected confidence sets, not for the graph-explicit incidence theorem.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The theorem is complete only for graphs with one substantively informative hazard \(S_k=\{j\}\), \(j\in\{k,k+1\}\), and all other \(S_t\) empty. It does not assert that this graph family is inclusion-maximal. Interacting hazards can create overlapping-parent constraints, positive-scaling recoveries on singular strata, alphabet-sensitive bridges, endpoint-only cancellations, and countermodel-gluing problems not addressed by the finite incidence scan; an arbitrary-local-graph recovery-or-obstruction calculus, its termination proof, and its positive gluing theorem remain future work.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The completed field claim is an arbitrary-horizon necessary-and-sufficient design theorem for the full single-informative-hazard subclass. It covers every specified finite alphabet with at least two states per visit, every positive substantive and response law, null effects on allowed arrows, and deficient transition ranks. It supplies an evaluable reconstruction, a legal positive countermodel on failure, and the exact minimal frontier, but makes no claim for graphs with two or more substantively informative hazards and no claim that the subclass is inclusion-maximal. No shadow-variable rank, parametric selection, missing-at-random, or faithfulness assumption is imposed, and no polynomial-time guarantee is claimed. Global projected confidence sets remain valid for all designs, including insufficient ones.
